summary: Preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute a large obfuscated sibling payload
details: @servicetitan/anvil-token@0.4.7 declares a `preinstall` hook (setup.mjs) that downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases (https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<bun-target>.zip) into a temp directory, extracts it, chmod +x's the `bun` binary, and then uses that freshly-dropped alternate runtime to execute a sibling file `math_init.js` via `execFileSync(bunPath, [math_init.js], { stdio: 'inherit' })`. The `math_init.js` file is a 727KB single-line bundle marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` and is heavily obfuscated: a shuffled string/numeric constant array (`n7gIxM`) rotated by a `WV8StW` function, with hex-identifier symbol names (`_0xNNNN`) throughout. setup.mjs itself uses the same hex-identifier obfuscation. A design-token package has no legitimate reason to fetch a language runtime at install time and execute a heavily obfuscated 727KB sibling under it. The alternate-runtime pattern is an evasion technique: the payload is never loaded by Node, so scanners that only inspect Node-resolved code do not see the executed behavior. On `npm install`, arbitrary code from the obfuscated payload runs on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
